name: Larry Hao
summary: Larry Hao (Zhuoyuan Hao) studies how LLMs reason and how RL systems fail. He is first author of Echoes as Anchors (ICLR 2026), co-first author of CHERRL, and a builder of agent systems for observable and controllable AI.
research_positioning: Make hidden model behavior measurable, then test it with controlled interventions: attention and causal trace analysis for LLM reasoning; known bias injection and ground-truth onset detection for reward hacking in rubric-based RL.

featured_research.title: Echoes as Anchors: Probabilistic Costs and Attention Refocusing in LLM Reasoning
featured_research.question_answered: Why do reasoning models repeat the prompt, and do those tokens perform functional computational work?

featured_research.title: Reproducing, Analyzing, and Detecting Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
featured_research.question_answered: How can reward hacking in rubric-based RL be reproduced with known ground truth and detected from training traces?
